basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 45-46.' and it opens 'VERS. 45, 46.-- Tulit itaque Jacob lapidem, et erexit illum in titulum, dixitque'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 45, 46.-- Tulit itaque Jacob lapidem, et erexit illum in titulum, dixitque fratribus suis: Afferte lapides, et reliqua. Quaeritur quare constituit Jacob lapidem super titulum? Sed diligenter advertendum [Z., animadvertendum] est quod istos titulos in rei cujusque testimonio constituebant, non ut eos pro diis colerent, sed ut eis aliquid significarent.
